  • Idefirix was generally well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with previous clinical trial experience

LUND, Sweden, October 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hansa Biopharma AB, "Hansa" (Nasdaq Stockholm: HNSA), today announced that data from the European Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES) study of Idefirix® (imlifidase) were presented during the High-Impact Clinical Trials oral session at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The abstract "FR-OR103 Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES): An Open-Label Post-Authorization Trial of 50 Imlifidase Crossmatch-Positive Deceased-Donor Kidney Transplants in Europe" was selected as a Late-Breaking Abstract at the congress.

Renée Aguiar-Lucander, CEO of Hansa Biopharma, said: "The presentation of the PAES study in the High-Impact Clinical Trials session highlights the scientific and clinical relevance of these findings and the potential of imlifidase to address a significant unmet need for highly sensitized patients awaiting kidney transplantation. We are encouraged by the continued interest from the transplant community in the growing body of evidence supporting imlifidase."

Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain and investigator for the trial said: "The successful completion of the PAES study provides important evidence in a patient population that continues to face significant challenges in accessing kidney transplantation. These findings add to the clinical evidence supporting the use of imlifidase to enable transplantation in highly sensitized patients with a positive crossmatch against a deceased donor."

ASN Kidney Week is one of the world's leading scientific meetings in nephrology and transplantation, bringing together researchers and clinicians to present the latest advances in kidney disease and transplantation medicine. The High-Impact Clinical Trials session features selected studies considered to represent some of the most clinically relevant and impactful research presented at the congress.

The abstract was presented by Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain, on behalf of the PAES study investigators.

Summary of the Abstract

Background

Imlifidase have a conditional approval in Europe since 2020. PAES (NCT05369975) is a controlled, non-randomized, open-label post-authorization efficacy and safety trial, designed to provide comprehensive data to support a full marketing authorisation of imlifidase (Idefirix®) in Europe.

Methods

Fifty highly sensitized (HS) patients who received crossmatch positive kidney offers received imlifidase treatment in line with the mode-of-action i.e. conversion of a positive crossmatch to a negative crossmatch and thereby enabling transplantation. All patients were unlikely to be transplanted under available kidney allocation systems, including prioritization programs for HS patients.

The primary trial objective was to assess graft failure-free survival at 1 year after transplantation. Secondary outcomes at 1 year includes kidney function assessed by eGFR, patient survival, graft survival, delayed graft function (DGF), antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) and safety.

Results

  • The graft failure-free survival was 90% at 1 year after transplantation in patients desensitized with imlifidase (n=50).
  • Graft and patient survival were 92% and 98%, respectively.
  • The mean eGFR calculated by MDRD was 51.04 mL/min/1.73 m2 (n=45).
  • DGF was seen in 40% of patients with a median duration of 14 days.
  • AMR occurred in 56% of recipients; however, no allograft loss was associated with AMR.
  • There were no new or additional safety signals found, and no imlifidase infusions were stopped due to infusion reactions.

Conclusion

Imlifidase enables kidney transplantation with a successful kidney function measured as eGFR at 1 year in patients desensitized. Imlifidase was well tolerated, with a safety profile consistent with prior experience and no unexpected or unacceptable risks observed.

Information about the trial is available at ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05369975

Notes to editors

About highly sensitized patients

Highly sensitized patients have pre-formed antibodies with a broad reactivity against human leukocyte antigens (HLAs). Those antibodies can cause damage to a transplanted organ and potentially graft loss.1 The presence of HLA antibodies means that highly sensitized patients have limited or no access to transplantation, as finding a compatible donor organ 

is particularly challenging.2,3 The immunological complexity of highly sensitized patients make them spend a longer time on transplant waiting lists, with an increased risk of dying while waiting for a suitable donor organ.4,5 Across the U.S. and Europe, highly sensitized patients comprise around 10-15% of all patients on transplant waiting lists.6,7

About Idefirix® (imlifidase)

Imlifidase is an antibody-cleaving enzyme originating from Streptococcus pyogenes that specifically cleaves and inactivates all immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody subclasses, including HLAs. It has a rapid onset and inactivates IgG-antibodies within hours after administration. The decrease in antibody levels creates a temporal antibody-free window of opportunity for highly sensitised patients to undergo transplant, thus enabling successful transplantation from an otherwise incompatible donor.

Imlifidase received a conditional marketing authorization valid throughout the European Union on 25 August 2020 and is marketed under the trade name Idefirix for the desensitization treatment of highly sensitized adult kidney transplant patients with a positive crossmatch against an available deceased donor. The use of Idefirix should be reserved for patients who are unlikely to be transplanted under the available kidney allocation system, including prioritization programs for highly sensitized patients.

The efficacy and safety of imlifidase as a pre-transplant treatment to reduce donor-specific IgG antibodies was studied in four phase 2 single-arm, studies in EU and US, a controlled Phase 3 study in US and in this European Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES) study. 5,7,10-11 .

Full EU product information can be accessed via the initial Summary of Product Characteristics found here

Idefirix is exclusively out-licensed for transplantation in EU, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Iceland and Middle East and North Africa (MENA) to SERB Pharmaceuticals since July 1, 2026.

In the US, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) accepted the Biologics License Application (BLA) for imlifidase in February of 2026 and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) action date of December 19, 2026.

About kidney failure

Kidney disease can progress to kidney failure or End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), identified when a patient's kidney function is less than 15%.12 ESRD poses a significant health burden, affecting nearly 2.5 million patients worldwide.12 A kidney transplant is the treatment of choice for suitable patients with ESRD because it offers improved survival and quality of life benefits, and is cost savings compared to long-term dialysis. There are approximately 170,000 kidney patients in the U.S. and Europe waiting for a new kidney.13

About Hansa Biopharma

Hansa Biopharma AB is a pioneering commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing and commercializing novel immunomodulatory therapies to transform care for patients with acute or complex immune disorders. Hansa's proprietary IgG-cleaving enzyme technology platform addresses serious unmet medical needs in transplantation, gene therapy and autoimmune diseases. The company's portfolio includes imlifidase, a first-in-class immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody-cleaving enzyme therapy, which has been shown to enable kidney transplantation in highly sensitized patients, and HNSA-5487, a next-generation IgG-cleaving molecule that will be developed for Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS). Hansa Biopharma is based in Lund, Sweden, and has operations in Europe and the U.S. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm under the ticker HNSA. data.description:
Vertex plans an at-home autoinjector launch if povetacicept receives FDA approval.

See more from StockTitan in Google Search and AI answers.Adds StockTitan as a preferred source · opens Google
Add on Google

- Vertex is on track for the U.S. FDA Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) date of November 30 for potential accelerated approval of povetacicept –

- Data published in NEJM and presented at ASN highlight povetacicept’s unique trifecta of efficacy, favorable safety, and the simplicity of dosing at-home every 4 weeks with a low-volume autoinjector –

- Data presented at ASN include a qualitative study examining patient perspectives on current and emerging IgAN therapies, showing that 96% of participants preferred an autoinjector over a prefilled syringe, and 80% of participants preferred dosing every 4 weeks versus weekly dosing -

- New clinical studies of povetacicept underway including a study evaluating patient experience on povetacicept administered via autoinjector -

BOSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated (Nasdaq: VRTX) today announced the publication of Phase 3 RAINIER results for povetacicept in the New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM), presentation of these data at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, Colorado, and advancement of the povetacicept clinical research program in IgAN. Vertex will also host an investor event during ASN on October 23 at 6:15-7 p.m. MDT (8:15-9 p.m. EDT). Further details are below.

Data being presented include a pre-specified Week 36 interim analysis of the ongoing Phase 3 RAINIER trial of povetacicept, an engineered fusion protein and dual inhibitor of the BAFF (B cell activating factor) and APRIL (a proliferation inducing ligand) cytokines, in immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). RAINIER met its primary endpoint, with povetacicept achieving a 52.0% reduction from baseline in proteinuria at Week 36 and a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 49.8% reduction versus placebo (P<0.0001), while also meeting both secondary endpoints.

The Week 36 interim analysis of RAINIER demonstrated that the depth of proteinuria reduction from baseline was consistent across demographic, clinical and regional subgroups, including an unprecedented 54.2% reduction in urine protein to creatinine ratio (UPCR) versus placebo in North America. Additionally, findings showed that 42.2% of povetacicept-treated participants reached 24-hour UPCR <0.5 g/g, the threshold aligned with current Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guidelines, compared with only 6.2% on placebo. Importantly, these findings were observed on top of optimized supportive care in both treatment arms, including sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use in 65.8% of participants, which is among the highest reported of any contemporary IgAN trial.

“At just 36 weeks of treatment, povetacicept has delivered impressive efficacy results, together with favorable safety and convenient dosing at-home every 4 weeks in a low-volume auto-injector that can fit into the lives of IgAN patients, underscoring the potential of povetacicept to substantially impact and redefine expectations for disease control in IgAN,” said Carmen Bozic, M.D., Executive Vice President, Global Medicines Development and Medical Affairs, and Chief Medical Officer at Vertex. “We are grateful to the patients, investigators, and study teams who made RAINIER the largest and fastest-enrolling contemporary IgAN trial to date and look forward to the November 30th PDUFA target action date.”

“What stands out from the RAINIER results is the important clinical validation of simultaneously targeting BAFF and APRIL to address upstream drivers and kidney injury in IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept was specifically designed as a high-potency, high-affinity TACI fusion protein with broad tissue distribution to deliver this dual inhibition in order to target upstream pathogenic immune complex production,” said Richard Lafayette, M.D., Professor of Medicine (Nephrology) at Stanford University Medical Center and RAINIER Steering Committee Co-Chair, who presented the data at ASN Kidney Week. “The results observed with povetacicept are among the most compelling I have seen in IgAN and highlight the potential of povetacicept to become an important new treatment option for patients living with this chronic progressive disease.”

Vertex also presented findings from a qualitative study examining patient perspectives on the device design and administration of current and emerging IgAN therapies, “Patient Perceptions of Injectable Therapies Among Adults with IgAN: A Qualitative Study” (#TH-PO0473). The study included in-depth, one-on-one interviews with 25 U.S. adults living with IgAN. Participants were shown pictures and short videos of the devices and asked to assess key treatment administration-related attributes. Findings showed that 96% of participants (24 of 25) preferred the characteristics of an autoinjector over a prefilled syringe, citing features such as the needle not being visible and elimination of manual needle insertion. Additionally, 80% of patients (20 of 25) preferred dosing every 4 weeks versus weekly dosing, with the top reasons being convenience and travel or time away from home considerations.

Vertex also announced a new clinical trial underway for povetacicept:

  • PAVANT IgAN Patient Experience Study (NCT07890909), A Phase 3b, Open-label, Single-arm, Patient Experience Study of Povetacicept Injection (via Autoinjector) in Adults With Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy

Visit news.vrtx.com/kidney-congress for more information about Vertex’s presence at ASN Kidney Week 2026.

Investor Event

Vertex will host an investor event and webcast on October 23 at 6:15-7 p.m. MDT (8:15-9 p.m. EDT) in Denver, Colorado, to discuss the data for povetacicept in IgAN, the Company’s program in APOL1- mediated kidney disease (AMKD), and other highlights across its kidney disease portfolio.

A live webcast of the presentation and Q&A portions can be accessed through the Investor Relations section of Vertex's website at investors.vrtx.com. To ensure a timely connection, it is recommended that participants register at least 15 minutes prior to the scheduled webcast. An archived webcast will be available on the company's website in the “Investors” section.

About RAINIER

RAINIER (NCT06564142) is a global Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pivotal trial of povetacicept 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks versus placebo on top of standard of care in 605 adults with IgAN (N=557 in main cohort, N=48 in the exploratory cohort). The trial was designed to have a pre-planned interim analysis evaluating the percent change from baseline in UPCR for the povetacicept arm versus placebo after a pre-specified number of patients reach 36 weeks of treatment. Final analysis will occur at two years of treatment, with a primary endpoint of total estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope through Week 104. RAINIER is the largest trial conducted in IgAN and achieved full enrollment faster than any contemporary IgAN trial.

As previously reported, patients treated with povetacicept achieved a 52.0% reduction from baseline in 24-hour UPCR at Week 36, with a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction of 49.8% in 24-hour UPCR compared to placebo (P<0.0001).

The trial also met its secondary objective. For the first secondary endpoint, patients treated with povetacicept demonstrated a 77.4% reduction from baseline in serum galactose deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1) compared to an increase of +9.1% in the placebo group, yielding a reduction of 79.3% compared to placebo (P<0.0001). For the second secondary endpoint, in patients with baseline hematuria, 85.1% achieved hematuria resolution in the povetacicept treatment group compared to 23.4% in the placebo group, resulting in hematuria resolution of 61.7% compared to placebo (P<0.0001).

Povetacicept was generally safe and well tolerated. The majority of adverse events (AEs) were mild to moderate. The most common events (≥10% of participants in either treatment group) for the povetacicept group versus the placebo group were upper respiratory tract infection (18.3% vs 11.4%), nasopharyngitis (9.7% vs 12.4%), and injection site reactions (14.5% vs 2.2%). There were no serious adverse events (SAEs) related to povetacicept and no deaths in the trial. There were no opportunistic infections, and no discontinuations due to infections. As expected, anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) were observed; these ADAs had no impact on efficacy or the risk profile.

Results from the RAINIER trial support the Biologics License Application (BLA) for povetacicept, which has been accepted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for accelerated approval in adults with IgAN. The Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date is November 30, 2026.

The RAINIER trial continues in a blinded manner until the last patient enrolled completes 104 weeks. Patients in RAINIER who have completed the Week 104 visit are eligible to enroll in the open-label extension study (NCT07807995), “A Phase 3 Open-Label Study of Long-term Treatment With Povetacicept in Adults With Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy,” and receive an additional 104 weeks of treatment and follow-up.

About Povetacicept

Povetacicept is a dual inhibitor of the BAFF and APRIL cytokines, which promote B cell activation, differentiation and/or survival, and provides B cell control by inhibiting the ability of BAFF and APRIL to drive the pathogenesis of multiple immune-mediated diseases. Due to its engineered TACI domain, povetacicept has demonstrated improved binding affinity, potency, pharmacokinetics, and/or tissue distribution compared to other APRIL, BAFF, and dual BAFF+APRIL inhibitors in preclinical studies.

If povetacicept is approved by the FDA, Vertex plans to launch povetacicept as a low-volume (<0.5 mL) subcutaneous autoinjector delivered once every 4 weeks via at-home administration.

IgAN is the first of multiple indications that Vertex is exploring for povetacicept given its pipeline-in-a-product potential. There are ongoing studies including the Phase 2/3 OLYMPUS trial (NCT07204275) in primary membranous nephropathy (pMN) and the Phase 2 ETNA trial (NCT07501702) in generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG).

About IgA Nephropathy (IgAN)

IgAN is a serious, progressive, life-threatening kidney disease driven by uncontrolled autoreactive B cell activity and is the most common cause of primary glomerulonephritis, affecting approximately 330,000 people in the United States and Europe and more than 1.5 million globally. IgAN results from the deposition of circulating immune complexes, consisting of immunoglobulins and galactose-deficient immunoglobulin A (Gd-IgA1), in the renal glomerular mesangium, triggering kidney injury and fibrosis.

About Vertex

Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases and conditions. The company has approved therapies for cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia, acute pain and acromegaly, and it continues to advance clinical and research programs in these areas. Vertex also has a robust clinical pipeline of investigational therapies across a range of modalities in other serious diseases where it has deep insight into causal human biology, including IgA nephropathy, neuropathic pain, APOL1-mediated kidney disease, primary membranous nephropathy, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent Cushing's syndrome, autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, type 1 diabetes, generalized myasthenia gravis, and myotonic dystrophy type 1.

Vertex was founded in 1989 and has its global headquarters in Boston, with international headquarters in London. Additionally, the company has research and development sites and commercial offices in North America, Europe, Australia, Latin America and the Middle East. Vertex is consistently recognized as one of the industry's top places to work, including 17 consecutive years on Science magazine's Top Employers list and one of Fortune’s 100 Best Companies to Work For. – Sefaxersen achieved a statistically significant 43.1% reduction in proteinuria, a key indicator of kidney damage, relative to placebo at 37 weeks with consistent treatment effects across all prespecified patient subgroups –

– Sefaxersen inhibits complement factor B production and has the potential to reduce kidney inflammation and slow IgAN disease progression –

– Investigational sefaxersen is intended to be a once-monthly subcutaneous injection and designed to enable convenient self-administration at home –

– Despite recent advances, many people with IgAN remain at risk of disease progression and kidney failure, highlighting the need for additional targeted treatment options for those who do not respond to initial therapy –

CARLSBAD, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: IONS) partner Roche announced today late-breaking oral presentation data from the ongoing Phase 3 IMAgINATION study in adults with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN) receiving optimized standard of care, demonstrating that investigational sefaxersen achieved a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 43.1% reduction in proteinuria (95% confidence interval [CI]: 32.5 - 52.0, P<0.0001), relative to placebo at 37 weeks, as measured by 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR). Proteinuria is a key indicator of kidney damage and a reduction in UPCR is strongly associated with the preservation of long-term kidney function. Results presented at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 also showed that, among patients with baseline hematuria (blood in urine), a greater proportion of patients achieved hematuria resolution at Week 37 with sefaxersen versus placebo.

"These data support our belief that sefaxersen is uniquely positioned to treat IgA nephropathy, demonstrating significant and clinically meaningful reduction in proteinuria and offering the potential to help reduce the need for long-term dialysis or kidney transplantation,” said Brett P. Monia, Ph.D., chief executive officer, Ionis. “Sefaxersen is a powerful example of the broad impact of Ionis' innovative science, and based on these results, we believe it has the potential to be an important new treatment option for people living with IgA nephropathy."

The treatment effect in all prespecified subgroups was consistent with the clinically meaningful reductions in proteinuria shown in the primary endpoint results. Sefaxersen was well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with the previously reported Phase 2 study, exhibiting no new safety signals.

Sefaxersen is an investigational once-monthly subcutaneous injection designed to enable self-administration for people with IgAN. The IMAgINATION study will continue as a blinded study to evaluate the change in kidney function over two years, as measured by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 105. Roche will share data with health authorities, with the goal of bringing this treatment to patients as soon as possible.

Typically diagnosed before the age of 40, IgAN affects at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year. IgAN, also known as Berger’s disease, is a chronic and progressive autoimmune disease that leads to end-stage kidney disease in up to 50% of patients within 20 years of diagnosis. It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis (inflammation of the tiny filters, glomeruli, in the kidneys) and is a major cause of chronic kidney disease as well as kidney failure.

Roche licensed sefaxersen from Ionis for the treatment of complement-mediated diseases. Under the terms of the agreement, Ionis received an upfront payment, license fee and development milestone payments and is eligible to receive regulatory and sales milestone payments as well as tiered royalties on net sales of sefaxersen.

About sefaxersen

Sefaxersen, an investigational, highly specific liver-directed antisense oligonucleotide that inhibits factor B production, is the first RNA-targeted therapy for IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Serum complement factor B levels are elevated in people with IgAN. Sefaxersen is designed to provide sustained control of the alternative complement pathway, an important pathway in IgAN, enabling once-monthly subcutaneous dosing and is intended for self-administration in people with IgAN.

About the IMAgINATION Study

IMAgINATION (NCT05797610) is a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous sefaxersen, an investigational antisense inhibitor of complement factor B, in patients with primary IgA nephropathy at high risk of progression. The study enrolled 459 people, who are randomized 1:1 to receive sefaxersen or placebo for 105 weeks. Participants may switch to open-label treatment after week 105 at the investigator's discretion or after the common-close timepoint, whichever occurs first. The primary endpoint of the study is the change from baseline in the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at 37 weeks.

About IgA Nephropathy (IgAN)

IgAN, also known as Berger’s disease, is a serious, chronic and progressive autoimmune kidney disease affecting at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year and is typically diagnosed before the age of 40 years. In IgAN, immune complexes deposit in the kidneys, which activates the complement system’s alternative pathway, leading to inflammation and subsequent kidney damage. It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis (inflammation of kidney glomeruli) and remains a leading cause of kidney failure, with up to 50% of patients experiencing end-stage kidney disease within 20 years of diagnosis. Many current therapies aim to reduce protein levels in the urine and control blood pressure to slow progression of the disease.

Updated KDIGO 2025 guidelines* highlight the need to address both the underlying immune-mediated causes of IgAN and the downstream consequences of kidney damage. While new therapies have expanded treatment options, important unmet needs remain, including improved long-term preservation of kidney function and more targeted approaches that address key drivers of disease progression.

  • Phase 3 RAINFOL™-02 trial met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) and its key secondary endpoint of overall survival (OS) with rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S®) compared to investigator’s choice chemotherapy
  • Results demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS and OS in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC)
  • Data will be submitted for presentation at a future medical meeting and discussed with regulatory authorities worldwide

COPENHAGEN, Denmark--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Genmab A/S (Nasdaq: GMAB) announced today positive topline results from the global Phase 3 RAINFOL™-02 trial of rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S®), an investigational folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeted, topoisomerase I (TOPO1)-inhibitor antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) regardless of FRα expression level or prior treatment with mirvetuximab. The trial met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS), with Rina-S demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement compared with investigator’s choice chemotherapy in the intent-to-treat (ITT) and in the primary analysis set (PAS) populations.

The ITT population (N=584) comprised of all randomized patients with PROC, regardless of FRα expression. The PAS population (N=492) mandated patients with FRα expression ≥75% PS2+ to have been treated with mirvetuximab.

In the ITT population, Rina-S demonstrated a 71% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death (HR 0.29; 95% CI, 0.23-0.37; p<0.0001). In the PAS population, Rina-S demonstrated a 67% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death (HR 0.33; 95% CI, 0.26–0.42; p<0.0001).

  • Sefaxersen achieved a statistically significant 43.1% reduction in proteinuria, a key indicator of kidney damage, relative to placebo at 37 weeks with consistent treatment effects across all prespecified patient subgroups1

Basel, 23 October 2026 - Roche (SIX: RO, ROP; OTCQX: RHHBY) announced today late-breaking oral presentation data from the ongoing phase III IMAgINATION study in adults with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN) receiving optimised standard of care, demonstrating that investigational sefaxersen achieved a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 43.1% reduction in proteinuria (95% confidence interval [CI]: 32.5 - 52.0, P<0.0001), relative to placebo at 37 weeks, as measured by 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR).1 Proteinuria is a key indicator of kidney damage and a reduction in UPCR is strongly associated with the preservation of long-term kidney function.6,7 Results presented at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 also showed that, among patients with baseline haematuria (blood in urine), a greater proportion of patients achieved haematuria resolution at Week 37 with sefaxersen versus placebo.1

“These phase III results demonstrate the potential for sefaxersen to meaningfully reduce protein in the urine, a key indicator of kidney damage, in people with IgA nephropathy,” said Levi Garraway, MD, PhD, Roche's Chief Medical Officer and Head of Global Product Development. “By inhibiting complement factor B in the liver, sefaxersen may offer a novel approach to slow disease progression in IgAN, potentially helping patients delay or avoid long-term dialysis or kidney transplantation.”

The treatment effect in all prespecified subgroups was consistent with the clinically meaningful reductions in proteinuria shown in the primary endpoint results.1 Sefaxersen was well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with the previously reported phase II study, exhibiting no new safety signals.1,2

Sefaxersen is an investigational once-monthly subcutaneous injection designed to enable convenient self-administration for people with IgAN.3 The IMAgINATION study will continue as a blinded study to evaluate the change in kidney function over two years, as measured by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 105. Data will be shared with health authorities, with the goal of bringing this treatment to patients as soon as possible.

Typically diagnosed before the age of 40, IgAN affects at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year.8,9 IgAN, also known as Berger’s disease, is a chronic and progressive autoimmune disease that leads to end-stage kidney disease in up to 50% of patients within 20 years of diagnosis.5,10 It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis (inflammation of the tiny filters, glomeruli, in the kidneys) and is a major cause of chronic kidney disease as well as kidney failure.8

About sefaxersen
Investigational sefaxersen is the first highly specific liver-directed antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) inhibitor of factor B production being evaluated in IgA nephropathy (IgAN).2 Serum complement factor B levels are elevated in people with IgAN. When we reduce these levels, it in turn reduces the level of protein in urine, which is a key indicator of improved kidney function.11,12

Sefaxersen is designed to provide sustained control of the alternative complement pathway, an important pathway in IgAN, enabling once-monthly subcutaneous dosing and is intended for self-administration in people with IgAN.3 In phase I and II trials, sefaxersen was shown to be generally well tolerated in healthy volunteers and people with IgAN who were at high risk of progression, and reduced proteinuria and plasma complement factor B.2,13

Roche licensed sefaxersen from Ionis Pharmaceuticals for the treatment of complement mediated diseases.

About the IMAgINATION study
IMAgINATION [NCT05797610] is a phase III, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous sefaxersen, an investigational antisense inhibitor of complement factor B, in patients with primary IgA nephropathy at high risk of progression.1,14 The study enrolled 459 people, who are randomised 1:1 to receive sefaxersen or placebo for 105 weeks.1,14 Participants may switch to open-label treatment after week 105 at the investigator's discretion or after the common-close timepoint, whichever occurs first.1,14 The primary endpoint of the study is the change from baseline in the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at 37 weeks.1,14

About primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN)
IgAN, also known as Berger’s disease, is a serious, chronic and progressive autoimmune kidney disease affecting at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year and is typically diagnosed before the age of 40 years.8-10 In IgAN, immune complexes deposit in the kidneys, which activates the complement system’s alternative pathway, leading to inflammation and subsequent kidney damage.15 It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis (inflammation of kidney glomeruli) and remains a leading cause of kidney failure, with up to 50% of patients experiencing end-stage kidney disease within 20 years of diagnosis.5,8 Many current therapies aim to reduce protein levels in the urine and control blood pressure to slow progression of the disease.16

Updated KDIGO 2025 guidelines* highlight the need to address both the underlying immune-mediated causes of IgAN and the downstream consequences of kidney damage.4 While new therapies have expanded treatment options, important unmet needs remain, including improved long-term preservation of kidney function and more targeted approaches that address key drivers of disease progression.4,16

For over two decades, Roche has advanced immune system research, creating groundbreaking targeted treatments that have transformed care for people with blood disorders, neurological conditions and autoimmune diseases. With a development pipeline exploring more than 20 medical approaches, we are targeting widespread, complex conditions like chronic lung disease (COPD) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), alongside lupus and autoimmune kidney diseases. Our ultimate goal is to lessen the burden of chronic immune disorders on patients, healthcare systems, and society.

SEC registration enables Cboe Clear U.S. to clear binary securities options alongside futures, positioning it to support innovation across the market

CHICAGO, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe: CBOE), a leading global markets operator and pioneer in equity and index derivatives, today announced that Cboe Clear U.S., LLC (CCUS) has received temporary registration from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to operate as a Covered Clearing Agency.

The registration expands CCUS's clearing capabilities beyond its existing authorities as a Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)-registered Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO) to clear securities products in addition to futures and swaps products. Together with recent enhancements to its regulatory framework and product scope, the milestone positions CCUS to support innovation and emerging opportunities across a broad range of assets and markets.

CCUS will initially use its SEC registration to clear Cboe's binary securities options tied to specified corporate key performance indicators (KPIs), which are planned to list on Cboe Options Exchange and be available on Robinhood in the fourth-quarter 2026. CCUS also recently received CFTC approval to clear margined futures broadly and continues to clear digital asset derivatives under its DCO designation.

"Clearing plays a critical role in bringing innovation to market," said Dale Michaels, Head of Cboe Clear U.S. "These expanded capabilities position Cboe Clear U.S. to become an innovation lane to support new products and meet evolving customer needs, while maintaining the rigorous risk management standards that are fundamental to our business."

These efforts complement Cboe's longstanding partnership with The Options Clearing Corporation (OCC)® and Cboe's continued commitment to supporting the established clearing infrastructure for traditional equity options.

The development builds on the growth of Cboe's established European clearing business, where Cboe Clear Europe has become the leading pan-European equities central counterparty, while expanding into new services such as securities financing transaction clearing. Together, these advances demonstrate Cboe's ability to extend its clearing capabilities across markets and asset classes.

To support its own future growth, CCUS has strengthened its infrastructure over the past year, including electing in June to become a Subpart C DCO. In doing so, CCUS is voluntarily adopting the enhanced standards the CFTC applies to systemically important DCOs for financial resources, risk management and operational resilience, aligning with those applied to leading global clearing organizations.

About Cboe Global Markets

Cboe Global Markets (Cboe: CBOE) is a leading global markets operator with a long history of innovation in equity and index derivatives. Since launching the world's first listed options exchange in 1973, Cboe has pioneered landmark products, including the introduction of S&P 500® index options and the creation of the VIX® Index, the world's leading gauge of market volatility, reshaping how investors manage risk and access opportunity. Today, Cboe operates derivatives, equities, and FX markets, providing trading, clearing, and investment solutions for customers worldwide. To learn more, visit www.cboe.com.

As one of the first platforms to integrate the newly released Kling 4.0 API, YouCam brings the full model to mobile and web, giving creators a new way to make AI videos that tell a full story.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Perfect Corp. (NYSE: PERF), a global leader in augmented reality (AR) and artificial intelligence (AI) beauty and fashion tech, today announced that YouCam is one of the first platforms to integrate the newly released Kling 4.0 API. The newest AI video model from Kuaishou Technology’s Kling AI is now live across the YouCam lineup on mobile and web. Built for longer storytelling, Kling 4.0 lets users set up to 10 keyframes instead of only a first and last frame, then generates up to 30 seconds of continuous video with lip-synced dialogue and stereo sound in a single pass.

YouCam Integrates Newly Released Kling 4.0 API to Turn Photos into 30-Second Stories with Dialogue and Sound

Kling 4.0 in YouCam at a Glance

  • Up to 10 keyframes: set the key moments of a story, like a storyboard
  • 30 seconds in one generation: twice the length of Kling 3.0, as one continuous take
  • Sound built in: dialogue, sound effects, and stereo audio come with the video
  • Multilingual speech: 9+ languages and several English accents, with matching lip movement
  • Mixed references: photos, character sheets, and video clips keep faces and products consistent
  • Trend remakes: reuse the pacing and shots of a reference video with new products and people

Plan the Story Before Generating the Video with Up to 10 Keyframes

Keyframes let users define what should appear at selected points in a video. Rather than describing an entire sequence in one prompt, users can establish its opening, intermediate moments, and ending, then provide instructions for movement and camera direction.

Kling 4.0 supports up to 10 keyframes and up to 30 seconds per generation in YouCam. These controls let users structure a short film scene, a product launch video, or a character-led story before generating it.

For example, an AI filmmaker can storyboard a 30-second scene in which a traveler steps off a night train, crosses a crowded platform, spots a stranger holding her lost suitcase, and stops face to face with him as the train pulls away. The keyframes fix each story beat in place, while the prompt describes the action, camera movement, and dialogue that connect them.

“The hardest part of AI video has been getting the model to follow your plan instead of guessing,” said Alice Chang, Founder & CEO of Perfect Corp. “Kling 4.0 lets YouCam users set up to 10 moments in a story and decide what each character says, so the video ends up the way they imagined it.”

Keep the Same Faces and Products in Every Shot

A longer story only works if its people and objects stay the same from scene to scene. Kling 4.0 accepts many kinds of references in one task, including photos, character sheets that show a person from several angles, storyboards, and short video clips that show how someone moves or how the camera should travel. The model uses them together to keep faces, outfits, and product details consistent throughout the video.

A consumer electronics brand can upload photos of its new wireless earbuds, a character sheet for its on-screen host, and a short clip showing the camera move it wants, then generate a launch video in which the earbuds and the host look the same in every scene.

Develop Dialogue Alongside the Visual Story

Every Kling 4.0 video can come with its own soundtrack. The model generates dialogue, background sound, and sound effects together with the picture, outputs them in two-channel stereo, and matches mouth movement to speech more closely than earlier Kling models.

Trend Remakes with a Reference Video

Users can also start from a video they like. With reference videos, such as a popular unboxing format, a travel vlog, or one of their own best-performing posts, Kling 4.0 follows its pacing, shot order, and presentation style, then replaces the products and people with the user’s own.

A brand can take one proven format and turn it into a separate video for every product in its lineup, and a video creator can join a trend with their own characters and story without planning every shot again.

The YouCam platform also includes a powerful web-based editor and a suite of developer APIs, providing creators, brands, and technology partners with seamless access to content creation capabilities across platforms.

For brands and professionals, Perfect Corp. offers an award-winning portfolio of enterprise technologies, including virtual try-on experiences for makeup, hair, jewelry, watches, and fashion accessories, as well as AI-powered skin and hair analysis.

  • Sigma Lithium extends the maturity of its 4-year US$100M senior secured debt with Synergy Capital by six months, from December 2026 to June 2027.
    • The interest rate on the senior secured facility remained unchanged at SOFR + 6.95% p.a., as did the covenants and events of default.
  • The extension defers Sigma Lithium's repayment by six months, enabling the Company to continue ramping up production and building operational cash flow before the new debt maturity date in June 2027.

  • Since operations restarted on October 5, 2026, the Company has produced 7,090t of lithium oxide concentrate up to October 22 , 2026.

  • Sigma Lithium maintains its target to scale its annualized production of lithium oxide concentrate to 330,000 tonnes by year-end 2027.

  • The extension follows a reduction in total debt over the past two years:

    • Repaid more than US$90M in debt since 2Q 24 through cash generation.
    • Reduced total debt by approximately 40% over the past two years, to US$125M as of October 21, 2026.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - October 23, 2026) - Sigma Lithium Corporation (NASDAQ: SGML) (ASX: SAU) (TSXV: SGML) (BVMF: S2GM34), the largest industrial-mineral lithium oxide concentrate producer in the Americas¹, dedicated to supplying global battery producers with sustainable and traceable lithium materials and its subsidiary, Sigma Mineracao S.A. ("Sigma Lithium" or the "Company") have signed an agreement letter to extend the maturity ("Extension Agreement") of its US$100 million in outstanding senior secured debt with Synergy Capital ("Synergy") by six months, from December 2026 to June 2027. The interest rate on the senior secured facility remained unchanged at SOFR + 6.95% p.a.

The extension defers the Company's debt final repayment requirement in December 2026, as a result enabling Sigma Lithium to lengthen 93% of its debt profile to June 2027, enhancing its financial flexibility, supporting its execution plans.

The extension gives the Company time to ramp up production following the restart of operations:

  • The Company recommenced operations on October 5, 2026, after the Federal Superior Court granted a decision reinstating all its environmental licenses.
  • The Company produced 7,090t of lithium oxide concentrate between October 5 and October 21, 2026.

Sigma Lithium maintains its target to scale its annualized production of lithium oxide concentrate to 330,000 tonnes by year-end 2027, supported by the Company's existing industrial capacity at its Cleantech Industrial Plant and its recycling and reprocessing circuits ("Cleantech Industrial Plant").

Sigma Lithium will report 3Q 26 production, sales, realized prices, costs and cash by November 13, 2026.

The extension follows a reduction in total debt over the past two years:

  • Repaid more than US$90M in debt since 2Q 24 through cash generation.
  • Reduced total debt by approximately 40% over the past two years, to US$125M as of October 21, 2026.

The Extension Agreement maintains similar covenants and events of default as the original senior secured debt agreement dated December 2022.

Ana Cabral, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Chairperson of Sigma Lithium, stated: "We appreciate the constructive engagement and continued support of Synergy Capital extending our maturity profile ahead of schedule. The six-month extension provides additional time to continue ramping up production ahead of the new maturity date. We have produced more than 6,400 tonnes of high-grade lithium oxide concentrate in the two weeks since operations resumed as we continue to ramp up production."

Ms. Cabral added, "Over the past two years, we have repaid more than US$90 million in debt. Together with our low costs and current lithium pricing levels, we expect to regain operational cash flow momentum. Thanks to the hard work of our teams and the trust of our stakeholders, our capital structure enhances our resilience and flexibility as we work toward our 2027 targets."

SIGMA LITHIUM IS AN ECONOMIC ENGINE IN THE JEQUITINHONHA VALLEY, ONE OF BRAZIL'S MOST DISADVANTAGED REGIONS

Sigma Lithium supports 19,000 jobs and approximately 80,000 family members. The Company's economic impact can be seen in the triple-digit GDP growth of towns in the Vale do Jequitinhonha (Lithium Valley), where it operates across 12 municipalities:

  • Araçuaí's GDP per capita grew by 123% and Itinga's by 110%, during the same period.
  • Araçuaí had the highest GDP per capita in the region, surpassing even larger municipalities such as Teófilo Otoni, which has a population four times larger.
  • Economic growth is further demonstrated by the opening of 9,410 new companies between January 2023 and March 2026.
  • Details of Sigma Lithium's social programs in the Vale do Jequitinhonha, including Dona de Mim, Zero Drought, Water for All and Education that Transforms, are available at https://sigmalithiumcorp.com/social/.

SIGMA LITHIUM HAS GENERATED SHARED PROSPERITY IN THE VALE DO JEQUITINHONHA

The scale of Sigma Lithium's social initiatives reflects their impact in the Vale do Jequitinhonha. These initiatives began before the Company commenced operations.

The Company has supported voluntary programs promoting economic inclusion, access to water, food security, education, and drought resilience since before it began generating revenue:

  • Dona de Mim: More than 2,000 women have become entrepreneurs through Sigma Lithium's microcredit opportunities, supporting approximately 10,000 family members.

  • Zero Drought: A total of 1,400 rainwater collection and irrigation structures ("Barraginhas") were built to strengthen drought resilience for approximately 5,600 small-scale subsistence farmers.

    • These initiatives support approximately 22,400 rural family members.
  • Water for All: Enabled access to drinking water for 100% of Sigma Lithium's neighboring community.
  • Education that Transforms: Sigma Lithium renovated and helped build local schools, sports facilities, and a childcare center, including a state-of-the-art SESI STEM school.

    • These initiatives support educational and extracurricular programs for approximately 776 children, expanding future opportunities for them and approximately 1,500 parents.

The Company runs one of the world's largest lithium production sites-the fifth largest industrial-mineral complex for lithium oxide concentrate-at its Grota do Cirilo operation in Brazil. Sigma Lithium currently has a nameplate capacity to industrialize 330,000 tonnes of lithium oxide concentrate on an annualized basis at its mine and state-of-the-art Cleantech Industrial Plant.
